issues.title: Printed RBS convergence and short-gap labels disagree

locations.anchor: K M_P A_P N_P convergence, positive roots tend to infinity
closure(Y_H) excludes e_infty(Q) when H is not contained in Q

issues.decisive_evidence: For upper P1=(1,2), g_t=diag(exp(2t),exp(-t),exp(-t)) has P1 adjoint root values exp(3t) and fixed unit Levi data, so the printed rule gives a fixed limit y in e_infty(P1). Exact successive minima are (exp(-t),exp(-t),exp(2t)), gaps (1,exp(-3t)), hence its tail lies in N_delta,delta'(P2,P2) for P2=(2,1). Neither parabolic contains the other and their flag dimensions prevent Gamma conjugacy. Every such closed cusp region contains y, contradicting both printed identifications.
issues.impact: Breaks the stated bridge from (8.3) to boundary masses in Theorem 1.2. Major proof identification problem even if repairable.
issues.repair_boundary: Unify opposite-parabolic/root and left/right quotient conventions; prove corrected closure limits and track the score coefficient. Mere relabeling without those checks is insufficient.
issues.counterevidence_limit: No invariant probability measure or entropy counterexample. Accumulation alone does not refute existence of an open neighborhood omitting the boundary point; only closed-set assertions are directly contradicted. Finite-scale Theorem 7.1 and Theorem 1.5 do not use this identification.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Section8.2 pp50-51 uses the K M_P A_P N_P convention with every positive relative root tending to infinity; pp52 and54 identify those RBS boundary labels with the dimensions of short lattice subspaces.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: For g_t=diag(exp(2t),exp(-t),exp(-t)), the printed Langlands convention gives convergence to the face P_(1,2), since its relative roots equal exp(3t). The ordered successive minima are exp(-t),exp(-t),exp(2t), with gap labels(1,exp(-3t)); the cusp definitions therefore place the same lattice in P_(2,1) for all sufficiently large t. These two parabolics are not conjugate in SL3(Z), since their stabilized subspaces have different dimensions. This directly contradicts the boundary-closure exclusion on p52 and the limsup identification on p54 under the source's own conventions.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The failure concerns the essential bridge from finite-scale entropy estimates to RBS boundary masses in Theorems1.1-1.2. It is not an invariant-measure entropy counterexample and does not prove that some correctly relabeled open cover or boundary theorem cannot exist. The finite-scale Theorem7.1 remains distinct.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Adopt a coherent left/right and opposite-parabolic convention, then re-prove the cusp-to-face identification and limit argument. A relabeling suggestion alone is not a verified replacement proof.

issues.title: Proposition 3.13 has an overbroad endpoint time quantifier
issues.decisive_evidence: For a_t=diag(exp(t),exp(-t)), x=diag(s,1/s)Z^2, s^2=eta0 exp(-2eps), delta=eta0 exp(-eps), t=2eps, the initial gap is below delta but final gap eta0 exp(2eps)>eta0. t/abs(log delta) tends to zero; choose eps sufficiently small that the short direction does not exchange.
issues.impact: Disproves the uniform all-delta statement near eta0.
issues.repair_boundary: Require delta sufficiently small, e.g. delta<=eta0^2 with a suitable time constant, or use a time proportional to log(eta0/delta).
issues.counterevidence_limit: Later applications take delta to zero and are not refuted.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Proposition3.13 p16 quantifies over every0<delta<eta0 with a uniform implied constant in |t|<<_a |log delta|.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: Take d2,a_t=diag(exp t,exp(-t)),x=diag(s,s^-1)Z?,s?=eta0 exp(-2epsilon),delta=eta0 exp(-epsilon),t=2epsilon. For small epsilon the short direction is unchanged, eta1(x)<delta but eta1(a_t x)=eta0 exp(2epsilon)>eta0, while t/|log delta| tends to0. Thus no uniform constant in the stated endpoint range works.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The singular-value bound eta_l(a_t x)<=exp(2||alpha||infty |t|)eta_l(x) proves the needed logarithmic margin for sufficiently small delta or a time proportional to log(eta0/delta). Actual asymptotic uses delta->0 can satisfy that corrected range.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Restrict delta to a sufficiently small fixed subrange or use the margin-dependent logarithm.

issues.title: Projected height increment has the opposite sign
issues.decisive_evidence: Correct Delta height=-|U| pi_P(alpha^w)+O(1). For a_t=diag(exp(t),exp(-t)), x=diag(exp(-L),exp(L))Z^2, U=[0,L/2], P=B, the printed subtraction has residual 2|U|alpha, unbounded with L.
issues.impact: Two displayed signed identities are incorrect.
issues.repair_boundary: Replace the relevant minus signs with plus signs.
issues.counterevidence_limit: The norms used by Corollaries 4.5 and 4.7 survive the overall sign reversal; no entropy-bound counterexample.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Equation3.4 p21 defines height with -log successive minima, while the estimate preceding Eq4.4 and Eq4.4 p23 subtract the projected height increment from the positive flow contribution.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: Using actual Proposition3.18 p20 yields Delta height=-|U|pi_P(alpha^w)+O(1). For the rank-two diagonal lattice diag(exp(-L),exp L)Z?, flow diag(exp t,exp(-t)), P=B and U=[0,L/2], the same short direction persists and the exact increment is -|U|alpha. The printed residual is2|U|alpha, unbounded as L grows.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The downstream estimates take the norm of the total vector sum, so correcting the sign retains their required cancellation bound. This does not require reversing the functional sign in the final entropy score.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Change the two local residual differences to sums consistently with the defined height.

issues.title: Window-dependent coding is not equivariant under the asserted enlargement

locations.anchor: Excursions are selected by a threshold hit within the observation window

issues.decisive_evidence: Let integer k large, a_t=diag(exp(t/100),exp(-t/100)), delta=exp(-1000k), delta'=exp(-250k), r=49/50, N=1100k, x=diag(exp(-474k),exp(474k))Z^2. Old log gap on [-N,N] ranges [-970k,-926k], never hitting delta or delta^r; coding is G. The new window for y=a_-N x corresponds to [-3300k,1100k], log gap [-1014k,-926k], hitting delta within a single delta' excursion; rerun coding is B. The formal translated C' remains G.
issues.impact: Refutes the stated set equality used to reduce the covering lemma to its forward form.
issues.repair_boundary: State the Lemma 6.3 induction for a prescribed partition with its continuous-time cusp properties, then translate the original labels directly. Retain the existing transition-count bounds.
issues.counterevidence_limit: C' belongs to C_2N because that is the set of all label functions. The covering exponent and entropy theorem are not refuted.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Lemma6.4 p44 equates a translated set of a prescribed finite-window coding with the set obtained by rerunning the canonical algorithm in the larger window. Definition13 permits all label-valued functions, so membership of the formal C' in its label space is not the issue.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: For sufficiently large integer k use a_t=diag(exp(t/100),exp(-t/100)),x=diag(exp(-474k),exp(474k))Z?,delta=exp(-1000k),delta'=exp(-250k),r=49/50,N=1100k. On[-N,N] the log gap lies in[-970k,-926k], never hitting delta or delta^r, hence the code is G. For y=a_-N x, its[-2N,2N] window corresponds to old times[-3300k,1100k], with log gap[-1014k,-926k]; it hits delta inside one delta' excursion and reruns as B, while the prescribed translated C' remains G. The printed set equality is false.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: Primary checked the actual pp43-44 induction and the helper's full alternative proof, not merely a repair slogan. For E=a_-N Z(C) use the common maximal integer intervals of the translated fixed code D(n)=C(n-N),0<=n<=2N. On each good interval the unit-time singular-value bound enlarges delta' only to K_a delta'; sufficiently small delta' gives V_l(a_s z)=a_s V_l(z) by the corrected Proposition3.13 range. Proposition2.2 pp8 and the nonrepeating ordered orientation intervals imply continuous interpolation of the same orientation between neighboring integer times. Thus every point of E has the prescribed continuous N^+_(K_a delta')(P,[w]) property on those common intervals. Proposition6.2 and the actual Lemma6.3 induction then give the same factor per interval and label-weight exponent without reusing the canonical coding equality. The original interval count, label counts and exceptional-duration bound are preserved; a_N converts forward2N balls to two-sidedN balls. The required K_a delta' remains in Proposition6.2's sufficiently small range. This supplies the actual covering conclusion and supports Minor despite the lemma's central use.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: State and prove the induction for prescribed common integer intervals with the continuous-time cusp property, use the bounded parameter enlargement just described, and translate that data directly. This interpolation argument is current acceptance reasoning, not a claim that it was already printed in the source.

issues.title: Adapted-basis block index and fixed-radius estimates need correction

locations.anchor: Equation (5.1), block number l versus dim Z_l
Proposition 6.2, wu2w^-1 in a Bowen ball of radius O(rho)

issues.decisive_evidence: (5.1): d=2, P=G, u=I, l=1, j=2 yields printed RHS 2z2 rather than z2. Correct start is dim(Z_l)+1. Proposition 5.3 only gives fixed epsilon0, while the p42 inference claims O(rho); u=I+c E21 under diag(exp(t),exp(-t)) has entry c exp(-2t), supremum c. The p53 score nonnegativity is justified by some phi<=0 (permutation average zero), not merely the printed phi>=0.
issues.impact: Local formula and scale bookkeeping errors in supporting proofs.
issues.repair_boundary: Correct block index. Cover a fixed small Bowen box with O_rho,epsilon0(1) small Bowen boxes; volume time factors cancel. Use the nonpositive functional orientation for score nonnegativity.
issues.counterevidence_limit: These repairs retain the claimed exponential covering rate; no new main theorem counterexample.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Equation5.1 p38 uses a block number where a cumulative dimension is needed; Proposition6.2 p42 treats a fixed epsilon0 bound as O(rho). The p53 nonnegativity justification cites the wrong functional sign.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: For d2,P=G,u=I,l1,j2, the printed sum beginning at l+1 adds the diagonal entry and returns2z2 instead ofz2; the correct start is dim Z_l+1. For u=I+cE21 under diag(exp t,exp(-t)), the supremum of its transverse entry over t>=0 is c, independent of rho. A fixed small Bowen box can instead be partitioned into O_(rho,epsilon0)(1) smaller boxes: the time-dependent coordinate contraction factors cancel in the volume ratio, so the additional factor is independent of T. Finally averaging projected alpha over all permutations is0, hence an orientation with phi<=0 exists and ensures h-phi>=0.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The corrected basis formula and fixed-box subdivision retain the required flag estimate and exponential covering rate. The final nonnegativity statement is true with the opposite choice of orientation; these local corrections do not repair the distinct RBS boundary mismatch.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Correct the cumulative block index, retain the fixed radius before subdividing, and choose the orientation with phi<=0 in the nonnegativity explanation.
